question.text: Which of Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, or Micron will post the highest percentage change in closing share price from the November 13, 2026 close to the November 27, 2026 close?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the option corresponding to the stock with the highest percentage change in closing share price from the November 13, 2026 close to the November 27, 2026 close, using the "Close" figures in the historical-prices tables published on Yahoo Finance for [Nvidia (NVDA)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/history/), [AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/history/), [Broadcom (AVGO)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AVGO/history/) and [Micron (MU)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/history/). For each stock the percentage change is (close on November 27, 2026 minus close on November 13, 2026) divided by (close on November 13, 2026), computed from the published closing prices without intermediate rounding. The highest value resolves the question, including when all four are negative (the smallest decline wins). If a Yahoo Finance page is unavailable or does not show one of the two required closing prices, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used to obtain that closing price.
question.fine_print: November 27, 2026 is a shortened US session that closes at 1:00 p.m. ET; the official closing price of that session is used, and extended-hours or after-hours trades do not count. If US markets do not hold a session on November 27, 2026, the closing prices from the next session in which all four stocks trade will be used instead. If two or more of the four stocks have exactly equal percentage changes, the question resolves to the tied stock listed earliest in the option order (Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron).

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 11.5 days. The end price is the 1 p.m. ET close on Friday, November 27, 2026, roughly 18:00-19:00 UTC that day. There are 9 trading sessions left, including the half day.

(b) **Status quo:** No session has traded since the November 13 baseline, so nobody is ahead. The only hint is Friday's after-hours trading, which does not count. There NVDA slipped -0.4%, against -2.5% to -3.2% for AMD, AVGO and MU. That gives NVDA a head start of about 2-3 points, which is small next to typical daily moves of 4-10%.

(c) **Base rates:** With four highly correlated names over two weeks, a naive prior is 25% each. In a race for the top return, the more volatile names win more often because their outcomes spread wider.
- AMD and MU have the widest recent swings, with single days of -17%, +13% and +12%.
- AVGO has been the steadiest of the four, up 0.2% over the past month. Lower volatility lowers its chance of finishing first.
- NVDA's day-to-day volatility is moderate, but it carries the biggest event risk: earnings, leadership news and government action.

A volatility-tilted prior is roughly AMD 28%, MU 27%, NVDA 25%, AVGO 20%.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **Nov 17, NVDA earnings:** 12 straight beats against a depressed share price. A beat plus solid guidance could spark a relief rally in a stock down 26% in a month.
- **Nov 15, Huang return chatter:** The FT reported Huang has discussed coming back, and an open letter backing him has more than 158,000 signatures. A return would be a large upside shock for NVDA.
- **Nov 15, Bessent pressure:** He called for an outside CEO and set a 10-day deadline around Nov 25 for the board to answer questions on China chip sales. This is downside tail risk for NVDA.
- **Nov 14-15, JPM AM note:** Nvidia's share of new frontier-lab compute deals has fallen to 39%, with AMD at 15%. This supports AMD's relative-strength story.
- **Through Nov 11, memory prices:** DRAM spot prices are softening while MU rallied hard, which raises MU's downside risk.
- **Nov 13, after-hours:** AMD, AVGO and MU all weakened more than NVDA, a slight positive for NVDA.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** Nvidia beats and guides strongly, and Huang is reinstated around Thanksgiving. NVDA rallies 15% or more while capital rotates out of AMD, which had been rallying on Nvidia's troubles, and NVDA wins. Alternatively, a broad AI selloff after NVDA's earnings would favor the low-volatility name, so AVGO wins by losing least.

**Adjustment:** Neither the research nor the markets point strongly in one direction. I moved NVDA up about 2 points for its after-hours head start and its two-sided event volatility, including the possibility of a Huang return. I moved MU down slightly because of the softening spot prices after its big run, and trimmed AVGO slightly for its lower volatility. No prediction market covers this exact question.
